laws.binds: Insurers, pharmacy benefit managers and other payers; drug manufacturers
laws.enforcement: The act names no penalty. The Insurance Commissioner writes the rules.

laws.summary: Insurers, pharmacy benefit managers and other payers may not pay a pharmacy less, add separate terms or claim modifiers, or leave it out of a network on the ground that it takes part in 340B. Drug manufacturers may not deny drugs to a pharmacy that contracts with a 340B entity.
laws.title: 340B Drug Pricing Nondiscrimination Act

AHCCCS and its contractors may not pay contract pharmacies for drugs dispensed as part of 340B. AHCCCS reports on whether the rule could reach hospitals.

laws.binds: Health insurers; pharmacy benefit managers
laws.limits: Applies to contracts issued, delivered or renewed on or after January 1, 2024. The state Medicaid agency (AHCCCS), its contractors and the AIDS drug assistance program are outside it.

laws.binds: 340B covered entities that bill Medi-Cal
laws.limits: Applies to Medi-Cal, the state Medicaid program, only.
laws.quote: A covered entity shall dispense only 340B drugs to Medi-Cal beneficiaries
laws.summary: A 340B covered entity dispenses only 340B drugs to Medi-Cal patients, bills Medi-Cal no more than its actual acquisition cost plus the set fee, and marks 340B drugs on its claims. Where it cannot buy a drug at the 340B price it may use another and keeps a record of that.

laws.binds: Pharmacy benefit managers
laws.limits: Does not apply to Medi-Cal or Medicare themselves; it does apply to pharmacy benefit managers that contract with managed care plans serving their members. Carried out only so far as it is consistent with the federal 340B law.

laws.summary: A pharmacy benefit manager may not set terms that treat a 340B covered entity, or a pharmacy it owns or contracts with, differently for covered drugs: lower or different payment, network exclusion, extra audits or steering patients away. It may not stop the entity from keeping the benefit of the discounted price.

laws.binds: Entities that meet the act's test of a 'prescription drug price manipulator'
laws.enforcement: An entity that does not meet the 98 percent rule can lose licences, state and local grants and its California tax-exempt status.
laws.limits: Reaches only an entity that meets every part of the test, among them spending over $100,000,000 on purposes other than direct patient care in a ten-year period and being an owner and operator of highly dangerous multifamily housing. Effective December 18, 2024 and operative January 1, 2025.

It sends a yearly accounting to state agencies.
laws.title: Protect Patients Now Act of 2024

laws.title: Colorado 340B Contract Pharmacy Protection Act

laws.summary: A manufacturer may not deny, restrict or prohibit delivery of 340B drugs to a pharmacy under contract with a covered entity; it may ask for claims data, up to three years back, to check for diversion and duplicate discounts.
